why: Production cards (pt-BR -> Japanese) had no answer key: the srs declaration named a deck, an item slug and a card type, but nothing said what the learner is asked and what counts as right. G1 of research/reports/readiness/srs_fsrs.md. Each row gives one card a prompt that identifies exactly one item in the whole corpus and an accept set that admits every legitimate surface of that item and nothing else.
definition: One row per (lesson, vocab slug) production card. prompt_pt is the pt-BR gloss of the sense the introducing lesson teaches, plus a disambiguator (part of speech, a short context cue, or the kana in parentheses as last resort) whenever that gloss is shared. accept lists the Japanese answers a grader must take: the headword, the orthographic kana (particles keep their spelling), the phonetic kana, every registry form and their NFKC twins - never a different word. sense_index records which sense of the vocab record the prompt is written from. why records the disambiguation decision when one was needed.
generated_by: W27 (authoring) of research/reports/APP_PLAN.md - per-batch authoring against corpus/vocab/*.json and the course srs declarations, then a global uniqueness pass over prompt_pt.
apply: W27 apply - writes card production keys into the srs declaration / card contract (W26) — ONLY rows with verified:true may be applied; the rest go back through a verifier.
